name: Spark Premium
tagline: Create a cross-platform focused email client with snooze, send later, and local search

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: Unlimited email accounts; Smart Inbox, smart notifications, essential productivity, calendar; no AI Meeting Notes quota disclosed for Free.
tiers.notes: Legacy Spark Premium is no longer the new public plan family; current public tiers are Free, Plus, Pro, and Enterprise.

tiers.name: Plus
tiers.limits: 40 AI Meeting Notes; advanced email productivity, Spark +AI/AI Assistant, custom templates, essential team collaboration.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: Unlimited AI Meeting Notes; Read Statuses, advanced team collaboration, HubSpot integration, Spark CLI; Workflows/Auto Labels/Drafts listed as coming soon.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Custom enterprise terms; numeric caps not published.

pricing.freeTierCaps: $0; unlimited email accounts; Smart Inbox, smart notifications, essential email productivity and calendar; no numeric send/storage cap disclosed.
pricing.hiddenCosts: Legacy Premium is not the current public upsell; AI Meeting Notes are capped at 40 on Plus and unlimited only on Pro.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Spark Premium, create a cross-platform focused email client with snooze, send later, and local search. The hard boundary is mobile and desktop apps, push, team drafts, sync, ai, and provider compatibility, plus mail infrastructure, integrations, and client polish.
coreLoopDIY: Connect an existing mailbox, index messages locally, provide a focused inbox with snooze, send later, and local search, and send through the account's normal SMTP service.
whatYouLose: mobile and desktop apps, push, team drafts, sync, AI, and provider compatibility
moatNotes: mail infrastructure, integrations, and client polish
ongoingBurden: IMAP quirks, OAuth, MIME, threading, search, attachments, offline sync, notifications, secure storage, and provider changes
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Spark Premium because an email client can be rebuilt; operating a trusted mail service with excellent deliverability cannot. The recurring cost buys IMAP quirks, OAuth, MIME, threading, search, attachments, offline sync, notifications, secure storage, and provider changes, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: mailcow
priorArt.desc: Popular open-source mail-server suite that demonstrates the operational complexity of hosted mail.

alternatives.name: Edison Mail
alternatives.desc: A free focused inbox with snooze, search and scheduled sending on Apple and Android; Windows gets less of the magic.

alternatives.name: Spark Free
alternatives.desc: The free plan already includes the described smart inbox, snooze, scheduled sends and search; Premium buys different things.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Mailspring
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Local search is free, but unlimited snooze and send-later still require Pro.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Premium Individual plan and a personal desktop mail client DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Spark Premium in an empty repository.
Use Tauri 2, React, TypeScript, SQLite, IMAP, SMTP, and OAuth where available; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: connect an existing mailbox, index messages locally, provide a focused inbox with snooze, send later, and local search, and send through the account's normal SMTP service.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Support one IMAP and SMTP account with credentials stored only in the OS keychain.
Index headers and message bodies locally with resumable sync and a visible status page.
Implement standards-based threading, folders, labels, archive, snooze, drafts, and search.
Render HTML email in a locked-down sandbox and block remote images by default.
Send multipart messages with attachments and preserve a local copy of every draft.
Add export, local cache reset, account reconnect, diagnostics, and safe logging.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out running a public mail server.
Deliberately leave out shared team inboxes and sales workflows.
Deliberately leave out mobile push services and provider-scale spam filtering.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
